public_rationale: This is a broad description, not a testable claim. Its core is a judgment about the future: that what Altman promises 'can't and likely won't' happen. A 'likely' judgment cannot be scored as true or false. He names no specific statements, period, or outlets. 'Meekly accepted' and 'without any real pushback' describe the tone of press coverage and have no measure. Any verdict would depend on which examples and outlets an evaluator picked, not on anything he said. So it is recorded as not adjudicable, not as true or false.
limitations: A narrower version naming specific Altman predictions with deadlines could be checked one by one, but that would be a different claim.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Altman has often claimed OpenAI or AI will do things it cannot and likely will not do, and the media has accepted these claims without real pushback.

statement.excerpt: There are many, many, many examples of him saying that OpenAI — or AI more broadly — will do something it can’t and likely won’t, and it being meekly accepted by the Fourth Estate without any real pushback.

from_speaker: him saying that OpenAI — or AI more broadly — will do something
meekly accepted by the Fourth Estate
our_interpretation: The claim has two parts. First, Altman often predicted things AI 'can't and likely won't' do. Second, the press accepted those predictions without real pushback.
'Likely won't' is a probability judgment about the future, not a fact that can be checked as of June 2024. 'Can't' is a claim about what is impossible, which present-day evidence cannot settle.
'Meekly accepted' and 'without any real pushback' have no measure. They would need a sample of media coverage and a standard for what counts as pushback, and he gives neither.
He names no specific statements, period, or outlets, so there is no fixed set of examples to test.
criteria.support_condition: Would need a set of specific Altman capability claims shown to be impossible or not realized, plus evidence that mainstream coverage repeated them without challenge. No plain reading gives a testable threshold for either part.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Would need evidence that Altman's capability claims were realized or plausible, or that major outlets routinely challenged them. Again, no plain reading gives a threshold.
